briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Fight Goes Political as Michigan Holds Steady — Psychedelics and M&A Momentum Build Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis market is proving tougher than the doom-and-gloom headlines suggested, with demand holding steady, Halloween product drops hitting shelves, and a gubernatorial nominee now vowing to kill the 24% wholesale tax. Nationally, Compass Pathways just opened its first U.S. office as psilocybin science matures, while fresh M&A activity and an October 13 DEA deadline keep rescheduling and consolidation squarely in play.

local.text: Bay City turns weed tax into warm beds — Commissioners are set to approve $150,000 in cannabis tax revenue to keep an overnight homeless drop-in center open for another year.
Michigan brands roll out boozy Halloween drops — Armada Cannabis launched spiked ciders including a 50mg THC blend and a live-rosin collab with Apex Solventless for the season.
GOP nominee pledges to kill the 24% tax — John James, endorsed by the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association, says he'll work to repeal or sharply reduce the wholesale tax if elected governor.

Demand holds steady despite the new tax — Dispensary sales are down only slightly in 2026, and analysts say oversupply, not the 24% levy, is driving lower prices, meaning shoppers haven't bolted to the illicit market.

Regulators clean house on bad actors — The state revoked 20 cultivation licenses and fined a company $2 million for shipping dirt labeled as marijuana, while also pulling Muha Meds' Ypsilanti license over a fake-customer scheme.

national.text: Compass Pathways opens its first U.S. office — The synthetic psilocybin company cut the ribbon on a Jersey City headquarters this week, with its COMP360 drug already holding FDA Breakthrough Therapy status.

Spherex doubles down with its first acquisition — Colorado's top cannabis brand is buying two cultivation facilities from The Cannabist Co., nearly doubling its workforce as it becomes vertically integrated.

New York dispensaries cross $4 billion in sales — State officials confirmed the adult-use market has now sold more than $4 billion in legal cannabis, a milestone for the fast-growing East Coast market.
Rove pushes into the Canadian market — The U.S. vape brand officially entered Ontario and plans to expand into additional provinces in the coming months.

Rescheduling hits a pause, not a dead end — A DEA judge stayed the Schedule III hearing to weigh a new GAO report, but the order doesn't reject rescheduling and sets an October 13 deadline for next steps.
